title: Polymer population and retained chain-length distribution
statement: A polymer distribution is the complete source-bound census of resolved chain carriers by repeat count and positive multiplicity, with number and mass weightings retained separately.
generation_rule: Generate the literal product of the eight registered binary coordinates; decide every form by complete carrier preservation, exact equivalence enumeration, minimality and absence of an extra rule.
grammar_boundary: Every finite observed polymer sample with complete chain identities, repeat counts, positive multiplicities, weighting rule, sample and method boundary.

choices.name: all-observed-chain-carriers
choices.reason: Every resolved chain enters the census.

choices.name: exact-chain-length-counts
choices.reason: Every carrier retains its repeat count.

choices.name: method-and-sample-bounded
choices.reason: Sampling and measurement boundaries are held.

choices.name: chain-population-trace
choices.reason: Every counted carrier and weight is retained.

choices.name: free-distribution-fit
choices.reason: A fitted shape can hide unfavorable chains.

choices.name: no-extra-rule
choices.reason: Complete population counting supplies the distribution.

induction_base: One finite sample with at least two resolved chain counts supplies the first distribution.
induction_step: Appending a chain increments exactly one retained length class or adds a new class without changing earlier multiplicities.
exclusions: no stereochemical dictionary, organic reaction taxonomy, polymer table, biomolecular database, measured target or V2 answer may select a candidate
no numerical zero, negative, irrational, imaginary or floating proof quantity
no free, fitted, learned or target-derived parameter
no atom, bond, orientation, repeat unit, chain or observation distinction may be created, copied or silently erased
absence is an Empty structural form rather than numerical zero
external target content remains inaccessible until the prediction is sealed
Every finite observed polymer sample with complete chain identities, repeat counts, positive multiplicities, weighting rule, sample and method boundary.
operational_witnesses: number and mass rules remain separate
falsification_condition: The claim fails if authority evidence lacks chain-length diversity, molar-mass distribution, distinct weightings or method boundary, or if a tampered row is accepted.
